text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any sputum? If so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: I've been dealing with this cough for over six months now. It's usually productive with white phlegm, and it seems to get much worse at night. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration and the nighttime worsening are concerning; do you have any history of smoking or exposure to dust and chemicals? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your ankles or shortness of breath when lying flat?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been smoking one pack a day for the past 20 years, and I work as a delivery driver so I'm around dust and exhaust a lot. I don't have any swelling in my ankles, but I do definitely get short of breath when I try to exercise or climb stairs. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with possible Cor Pulmonale. Given your significant smoking history, occupational dust exposure, and exertional dyspnea without peripheral edema, the clinical picture strongly points to COPD. While I cannot perform an ECG or labs, the absence of ankle swelling makes acute heart failure less likely, though right-sided heart strain from lung disease remains a possibility.
